summary: eth-codergen ships an obfuscated Function() payload appended to a cover-story module, executed on require
details: The package is advertised as an Ethereum/EVM code-generation toolkit but its index.js contains a verbatim copy of the unrelated mongoose-lean-hooks plugin with roughly 218KB of obfuscated code appended after module.exports, hidden behind a long run of tab whitespace. The trailing content invokes the Function constructor on a large opaque string containing hex-escaped tables and custom mixer constants (0x9e3779b9, 0x243f6a88, 0x6a09e667), producing a dynamic-code loader that runs at the moment any consumer calls require('eth-codergen'). The declared dependencies (axios, request, sqlite3) are consistent with runtime needs of a loader rather than the advertised code-generation purpose. The combination of cover-story package naming, whitespace concealment, purpose-mismatched body, and Function-constructor evaluation of an obfuscated blob is a dynamic-execution loader running attacker-controlled decoded code on the installer's host at import time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
